activity_share_transition_audit.purpose: Detect abrupt utilization switching that capacity stock and turnover assumptions alone may not prevent.
activity_share_transition_audit.method: Sum TotalAnnualTechnologyActivityByMode across modes, calculate each member's share of its stock class, and compare adjacent model years. No activity bound or activity share is imposed.
activity_share_transition_audit.interpretation: This is a diagnostic, not a pass/fail smoothness constraint. Remaining changes can reflect dispatch among already available stocks, demand-profile changes, or missing technology-specific utilization evidence.

heat_removal_regression.interpretation: Objective, demand, emissions, fixed cost and investment cost are invariants. Activity, zero-cost capacity, water-source routing and timeslice-level production/use may select a different cost-identical LP basis when redundant heat rows are removed; exact rows are retained in the comparisons.

diagnostic_history: Equation replay isolated the blanket PHL_POW_* 2020 capacity closure as the structural infeasibility; the source generator now preserves capacity-free pass-through technologies.
Full-precision result parsing plus one-part-per-million headroom removed a 3.91053e-06 services-heat balance shortfall caused by the rounded baseline CSV.

The corrected generic-UDC case timed out at 280 seconds; a controlled no-UDC rollback solved optimally in 125.35 seconds. A native permit-network source formulation also timed out at 280 seconds. The no-aggregate result showed >25-point annual share changes in five classes, so the final source uses full-horizon, uncoupled NCC1 technology-adoption bounds.
